subject: SLA anchor and monthly remedy cap — Lumina Health negotiation
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Wallace <tom.wallace@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed SLA anchor and monthly remedy cap (Lumina pilot)

Tom — thanks again for the conversation yesterday. As discussed, attaching a clean draft of the SLA we usually propose for pilot-to-prod customers. High level:

- Standard availability anchor: 99.95% monthly (applies per-region).
- Remedy: service credits tiered by monthly availability shortfall (see attached table).
- Monthly credit cap: 100% of monthly Redwood invoice for the affected service.
- Maintenance and emergency maintenance carveouts are called out (standard 4-hour window notification for planned maintenance).

I know Lumina is sensitive to clinical-impact availability. Two quick asks so I can bring a targeted proposal back:
1) Do you need a higher anchor (e.g., 99.98% or 99.99%) for any particular region/service?
2) Is the remedy cap of 100% acceptable, or would procurement need a higher cap/uncapped remedy for critical services?

We're open to structure: examples include raising the anchor for a specific EU region in exchange for a slightly higher monthly cap, or offering a failover routing assurance with an increased remedy cap but limited to core inference endpoints.

If you prefer, I can loop in our reliability lead (Ben) and legal (Laura) to draft targeted language.

Regards,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SLA-draft-Lumina-20270419.pdf (PDF, 12 pages)

------------------------------
From: Tom Wallace <tom.wallace@luminahealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@luminahealth.com
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed SLA anchor and monthly remedy cap (Lumina pilot)

Hannah — appreciate the draft and context. A few points from our side (procurement + platform ops):

- Lumina will be running inference on near-RT critical workflows (triage routing and med-scribe summaries). We need higher assurance: target anchor of 99.98% at minimum for US region; 99.99% preferred for primary cluster.
- Remedy cap: procurement signaled that a 100% cap doesn’t adequately mitigate risk for clinical workloads. We would ask that credits be uncapped for top-tier incidents impacting patient-facing endpoints, or alternatively a cap at 200% of monthly spend for incidents meeting the highest severity definition.
- Maintenance carveouts: acceptable if scheduled with 48 hours notice for production-impacting windows (not 4 hours).

Operational ask: before we move legal, can Redwood share a short runbook or failover diagram showing cross-region failover behavior and expected RTO/RPO for model endpoints? Also please attach the SOC 2 excerpt that covers change control and incident response.

Tom Wallace
Head of Platform Reliability
Lumina Health

------------------------------
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Wallace <tom.wallace@luminahealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed SLA anchor and monthly remedy cap (Lumina pilot)

Tom — thanks for the clear feedback. I’ve summarized a possible compromise below that balances Lumina’s clinical risk profile and Redwood’s operational guarantees: 

1) Availability anchor: we can offer a targeted 99.98% anchor for Lumina’s US-primary cluster (region scoped) during the initial 6‑month pilot-to-onboard period. The global/other-region anchor remains 99.95% unless otherwise negotiated.

2) Remedy cap: increase the monthly cap to 150% of the Redwood invoice for the affected service for incidents that meet our Severity-1 definition and where the incident is attributable to Redwood service availability (not third-party network or customer misconfiguration). 

3) Escalation carveouts: we will include a separate 'critical-path' carveout where, upon mutual verification of patient-impacting outage (both parties' on-call confirm), remedies are calculated with an escalated multiplier (up to the 150% cap) and we commit to a runbook-driven rollback/playbook. 

4) Maintenance notice: we can extend planned maintenance notice to 48 hours for production-impacting windows for Lumina’s primary cluster. Emergency maint windows remain subject to best-effort notice and post-facto reporting.

5) Evidence: attaching a short runbook excerpt and SOC 2 excerpt as requested. Ben (cc’d) will follow up with a short slide that explains our multi-AZ failover and expected RTO under the proposed configuration.

If this compromise looks reasonable from Lumina’s procurement and legal side, Laura can draft the targeted SLA language to be appended to the standard template. If not, tell me which single term is the blocker (anchor or cap) and we’ll escalate.

Thanks — will await your thoughts.

Hannah Schmitt
Director, Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference

Attachments: runbook-summary.pdf, SOC2-excerpt.pdf

------------------------------
From: Tom Wallace <tom.wallace@luminahealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@luminahealth.com
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed SLA anchor and monthly remedy cap (Lumina pilot)

Hannah — that compromise moves the conversation forward. Procurement will review the 150% cap vs uncapped ask; the 99.98% anchor for the US-primary cluster is acceptable as a pilot condition. Two follow-ups: 1) we’ll need the Ben slide for our reliability review before legal signs off; 2) procurement requests a short clause that allows Lumina to request a one-time waiver to the cap for a proved patient-impacting incident (we can accept that as a documented exception if mutually approved).

I’ll return a redline shortly after procurement review. Appreciate the quick turnaround and attachments.

Tom
Head of Platform Reliability, Lumina Health
